facts.statement: The genus Parasaurolophus was first described by William Parks in 1922.
facts.quote: authority: Parks, 1922

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus lived in western North America and possibly Asia during the Late Cretaceous period, approximately 76.5 to 73 million years ago.
facts.quote: Parasaurolophus (; meaning "beside crested lizard" in reference to Saurolophus) is a genus of hadrosaurid "duck-billed" dinosaur that lived in what is now western North America and possibly Asia during the Late Cretaceous period, about 76.5–73 million years ago.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus was a large herbivore reaching over 9 meters in length and weighing over 5 metric tons, capable of moving on two or four legs.
facts.quote: It was a large herbivore that could reach over 9 m long and weigh over 5 MT, and were able to move as a biped and a quadruped.

facts.statement: The type specimen, ROM 768, was found in 1920 near Sand Creek along the Red Deer River in Alberta by a University of Toronto field party.
facts.quote: It is based on ROM 768, a skull and partial skeleton missing most of the tail and the back legs below the knees, which was found by a field party from the University of Toronto in 1920 near Sand Creek along the Red Deer River in Alberta.

facts.statement: The type species P. walkeri was named by William Parks in honor of Sir Byron Edmund Walker.
facts.quote: William Parks named the specimen P. walkeri in honor of Sir Byron Edmund Walker, the chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Royal Ontario Museum.

facts.statement: A partial skull was recovered in 1921 by Charles H. Sternberg from the Kirtland Formation in New Mexico.
facts.quote: In 1921, Charles H. Sternberg recovered a partial skull (PMU.R1250) from what is now known as the slightly younger Kirtland Formation in San Juan County, New Mexico.

facts.statement: Carl Wiman described the New Mexico skull as the species P. tubicen in 1931.
facts.quote: This specimen was sent to Uppsala, where Carl Wiman described it as a second species, P. tubicen, in 1931.

facts.statement: John Ostrom described the specimen FMNH P27393 as P. cyrtocristatus in 1961.
facts.quote: John Ostrom described another good specimen (FMNH P27393) from New Mexico as P. cyrtocristatus in 1961.

facts.statement: David B. Weishampel and James A. Jensen described the range of P. cyrtocristatus in 1979 based on a skull found in Utah.
facts.quote: The range of this species was described in 1979, when David B. Weishampel and James A. Jensen described a partial skull with a similar crest (BYU 2467) from the Campanian age Kaiparowits Formation of Garfield County, Utah.

facts.statement: P. tubicen is the largest of the three recognized species of Parasaurolophus.
facts.quote: The next named species is P. tubicen, which is the largest of the Parasaurolophus species.

facts.statement: P. cyrtocristatus is the smallest species of Parasaurolophus and has the most curved crest.
facts.quote: Of the Parasaurolophus species, P. cyrtocristatus is the smallest and has the most curved crest.

facts.statement: It has been debated whether P. cyrtocristatus represents a female of P. walkeri or P. tubicen, though some studies argue against this due to differences in age and anatomy.
facts.quote: Because of its possession of the two above features, it has often been speculated that it was a female of P. walkeri or P. tubicen, which were all thought to be males, although P. tubicen lived approximately a million years later.

facts.statement: A 2014 study led by Xing suggested that Charonosaurus jiayensis should be classified as P. jiayensis, extending the genus's range to Asia and the K-Pg boundary.
facts.quote: A study published in PLoS ONE in 2014 found that one more species could be referred to Parasaurolophus. This study, led by Xing, found Charonosaurus jiayensis was actually nested deeply inside Parasaurolophus, which created the new species P. jiayensis.

facts.statement: The type specimen of P. walkeri is estimated to be 9.45 meters long, with a body mass exceeding 5 metric tons for a 9-meter individual.
facts.quote: The length of the type specimen of P. walkeri is estimated at 9.45 m, and allometry-based body mass estimates indicate that a 9 m long individual would have weighed more than 5 MT.

facts.statement: The skull of the P. walkeri type specimen, including the crest, measures about 1.6 meters in length.
facts.quote: The skull of the P. walkeri type specimen is about 1.6 m long, including the crest.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus could walk on two or four legs, likely preferring to forage quadrupedally but running bipedally.
facts.quote: Like other hadrosaurids, it was able to walk on either two legs or four. It probably preferred to forage for food on four legs, but ran on two.

facts.statement: Skin impressions of P. walkeri reveal uniform tubercle-like scales without larger structures.
facts.quote: Skin impressions are known for P. walkeri, showing uniform tubercle-like scales, but no larger structures.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus is characterized by a prominent cranial crest located at the back of the head, composed of the premaxilla and nasal bones.
facts.quote: The most noticeable feature was the cranial crest that protruded from the rear of the head and was made up of the premaxilla and nasal bones.

facts.statement: The crest of Parasaurolophus was hollow, containing tubes that connected the nostrils to the end of the crest and then back into the skull.
facts.quote: The crest was hollow, with distinct tubes leading from each nostril to the end of the crest before reversing direction and heading back down the crest and into the skull.

facts.statement: P. walkeri and P. tubicen possessed long, slightly curved crests, whereas P. cyrtocristatus had a short crest with a circular profile.
facts.quote: While P. walkeri and P. tubicen had long crests with slight curvature, P. cyrtocristatus had a short crest with a more circular profile.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus is classified as a member of the lambeosaurine subfamily within the hadrosaurids, distinct from the hadrosaurine Saurolophus.
facts.quote: However, it was soon reassessed as a member of the lambeosaurine subfamily of hadrosaurids—Saurolophus is a hadrosaurine.

facts.statement: The closest known relative of Parasaurolophus is Charonosaurus, a lambeosaurine from the Amur region of northeastern China that has a similar skull but lacks a complete crest.
facts.quote: Its closest known relative appears to be Charonosaurus, a lambeosaurine with a similar skull (but no complete crest yet) from the Amur region of northeastern China.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus and Charonosaurus may together form a clade named Parasaurolophini.
facts.quote: The two may form the clade called Parasaurolophini.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus was a large herbivore capable of moving on two or four legs, possessing a skull that allowed a grinding motion similar to chewing.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Parasaurolophus was a large bipedal and quadrupedal herbivore, eating plants with a sophisticated skull that permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus had dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth that were continuously replaced, with only a few in use at any given time.
facts.quote: Its teeth were continually being replaced and were packed into dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, but only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus could feed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to a height of approximately 4 meters.
facts.quote: Vegetation could have been taken from the ground up to a height of around 4 m.

facts.statement: A juvenile Parasaurolophus specimen, numbered RAM 14000 and nicknamed Joe, was described in 2013.
facts.quote: Parasaurolophus is known from many adult specimens, and a juvenile described in 2013, numbered RAM 14000 and nicknamed Joe, after a volunteer at the Raymond M. Alf Museum of Paleontology (RAM).

facts.statement: The juvenile Parasaurolophus specimen lived approximately 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: This individual fits neatly into the currently known Parasaurolophus growth stages, and lived approximately 75 million years ago.

facts.statement: At 25% of adult size, the juvenile Parasaurolophus shows that crest growth began earlier than in related genera like Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: At 25% of the total adult size, the juvenile show that crest growth of Parasaurolophus began sooner than in related genera, such as Corythosaurus.

facts.statement: Juvenile Parasaurolophus had a low, hemispherical crest, unlike the long and tubular crests of adults.
facts.quote: The crest of the juvenile is not long and tubular like the adults, but low and hemispherical.

facts.statement: Many hypotheses regarding the function of the Parasaurolophus cranial crest have been proposed, though most have been discredited.
facts.quote: Many hypotheses have been advanced as to what functions the cranial crest of Parasaurolophus performed, but most have been discredited.

facts.statement: Current theories suggest the Parasaurolophus crest served functions such as visual display, sound amplification, and thermoregulation.
facts.quote: It is now believed that it may have had several functions: visual display for identifying species and sex, sound amplification for communication, and thermoregulation.

facts.statement: It remains unclear which function of the Parasaurolophus crest was most significant during different stages of its evolution.
facts.quote: It is not clear which was most significant at what times in the evolution of the crest and its internal nasal passages.

facts.statement: James Hopson suggested that P. cyrtocristatus represented the female form of P. tubicen due to its smaller crest.
facts.quote: James Hopson, one of the first researchers to describe lambeosaurine crests in terms of such distinctions, suggested that P. cyrtocristatus, with its small crest, was the female form of P. tubicen.

facts.statement: Thomas Williamson proposed that P. cyrtocristatus was a juvenile form, but neither the female nor juvenile hypotheses gained widespread acceptance.
facts.quote: Thomas Williamson suggested it was the juvenile form. Neither hypothesis became widely accepted.

facts.statement: Research suggests juvenile Parasaurolophus likely had small, rounded crests similar to P. cyrtocristatus that grew rapidly as they approached sexual maturity.
facts.quote: Williamson noted that in any case, juvenile Parasaurolophus probably had small, rounded crests like P. cyrtocristatus, that probably grew faster as individuals approached sexual maturity.

facts.statement: Early researchers proposed that the crest of Parasaurolophus was an adaptation for an aquatic lifestyle, a hypothesis common until the 1960s.
facts.quote: Many early suggestions focused on adaptations for an aquatic lifestyle, following the hypothesis that hadrosaurids were amphibious, a common line of thought until the 1960s.

facts.statement: Alfred Sherwood Romer suggested the crest acted as a snorkel, while others proposed it was an attachment for a proboscis, an air trap, or an air reservoir for underwater stays.
facts.quote: Alfred Sherwood Romer proposed it served as a snorkel, Martin Wilfarth that it was an attachment for a mobile proboscis used as a breathing tube or for food gathering, Charles M. Sternberg that it served as an airtrap to keep water out of the lungs, and Ned Colbert that it served as an air reservoir for prolonged stays underwater.

facts.statement: In 1922, William Parks hypothesized that the crest was connected to shoulder vertebrae by ligaments or muscles to help support and move the head.
facts.quote: William Parks, in 1922, suggested that the crest was joined to the vertebrae above the shoulders by ligaments or muscles, and helped with moving and supporting the head.

facts.statement: Othenio Abel proposed the crest was used as a weapon in intraspecific combat, while Andrew Milner suggested it acted as a foliage deflector similar to a cassowary's casque.
facts.quote: Othenio Abel proposed it was used as a weapon in combat among members of the same species, and Andrew Milner suggested that it could be used as a foliage deflector, like the helmet crest (called a 'casque') of the cassowary.

facts.statement: Halszka Osmólska and John Ostrom proposed the crest housed salt glands or expanded olfactory tissue to improve the sense of smell.
facts.quote: Halszka Osmólska suggested that it housed salt glands, and John Ostrom suggested that it housed expanded areas for olfactory tissue and much improved sense of smell of the lambeosaurines, which had no obvious defensive capabilities.

facts.statement: Wiman suggested in 1931 that the crest acted as a resonating chamber similar to a swan's, using elongated nasal passages to create noise.
facts.quote: This function was originally suggested by Wiman in 1931 when he described P. tubicen. He noted that the crest's internal structures are similar to those of a swan and theorized that an animal could use its elongated nasal passages to create noise.

facts.statement: Weishampel in 1981 suggested Parasaurolophus produced noises between 55 and 720 Hz, with variations based on species, crest size, and nasal passage length.
facts.quote: Weishampel in 1981 suggested that Parasaurolophus made noises ranging between the frequencies 55 and 720 Hz, although there was some difference in the range of individual species because of the crest size, shape, and nasal passage length, most obvious in P. cyrtocristatus (interpreted as a possible female).

facts.statement: Computer modeling of a well-preserved P. tubicen specimen allowed researchers to reconstruct the possible sound produced by its crest.
facts.quote: Computer modeling of a well-preserved specimen of P. tubicen, with more complex air passages than those of P. walkeri, has allowed the reconstruction of the possible sound its crest produced.

facts.statement: Computer modeling indicates the main resonant frequency of the crest is around 30 Hz, with peaks and valleys caused by sinus anatomy.
facts.quote: The main path resonates at around 30 Hz, but the complicated sinus anatomy causes peaks and valleys in the sound.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown in 1912 hypothesized that fine striations near the crest were associated with a skin frill comparable to that of a modern basilisk lizard.
facts.quote: Barnum Brown (1912) noted the presence of fine striations near the back of the crest that he hypothesized could be associated with the presence of a frill of skin, comparable to the one found in the modern basilisk lizard.

facts.statement: A specimen of P. walkeri shows a V-shaped gap or notch in the vertebrae at the base of the neck, which might be a pathology.
facts.quote: P. walkeri is known from one specimen which might contain a pathology. The skeleton shows a v-shaped gap or notch in the vertebrae at the base of the neck.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus walkeri lived alongside diverse prehistoric animals in the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: Parasaurolophus walkeri, from the Dinosaur Park Formation, was a member of a diverse and well-documented fauna of prehistoric animals

facts.statement: The habitat of Parasaurolophus in the Dinosaur Park Formation was a low-relief area of rivers and floodplains that became swampy and influenced by marine conditions.
facts.quote: The Dinosaur Park Formation is interpreted as a low-relief setting of rivers and floodplains that became more swampy and influenced by marine conditions over time

facts.statement: The climate where Parasaurolophus lived was warmer than modern Alberta, without frost, but featuring wetter and drier seasons.
facts.quote: The climate was warmer than present-day Alberta, without frost, but with wetter and drier seasons

facts.statement: Some Parasaurolophus remains in the Dinosaur Park Formation may belong to individuals that died while migrating through the region.
facts.quote: Some of the less common hadrosaurs in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Dinosaur Provincial Park, such as Parasaurolophus, may represent the remains of individuals who died while migrating through the region

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus may have inhabited upland areas where it nested or fed.
facts.quote: They might also have had a more upland habitat where they may have nested or fed

facts.statement: When Parasaurolophus existed, the Fruitland Formation was a swampy lowland area close to the shore of the Cretaceous Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: When Parasaurolophus existed, the Fruitland Formation was swampy, positioned in the lowlands, and close to the shore of the Cretaceous Interior Seaway

facts.statement: The Fruitland Formation, where Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus lived, dates from just younger than 75.56 million years ago to 74.55 million years ago.
facts.quote: The lowermost part of the Fruitland Formation is just younger than 75.56 ± 0.41 mya, with the uppermost boundary dating to 74.55 ± 0.22 mya

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus tubicen lived slightly later than P. cyrtocristatus and is found in the Kirtland Formation of New Mexico.
facts.quote: Existing slightly later than the species from the Fruitland Formation, P. tubicen is also found in New Mexico, in the Kirtland Formation

facts.statement: The Kirtland Formation, home to Parasaurolophus tubicen, spans from 74.55 million years ago to around 73.05 million years ago.
facts.quote: The beginning of the Kirtland Formation dates to 74.55 ± 0.22 mya, with the formation ending at around 73.05 ± 0.25 mya

facts.statement: The plateau where Parasaurolophus lived was an ancient floodplain with large channels, wetland swamps, ponds, and lakes, bordered by highlands.
facts.quote: The plateau where dinosaurs lived was an ancient floodplain dominated by large channels and abundant wetland peat swamps, ponds and lakes, and was bordered by highlands

facts.statement: The climate of the Kaiparowits Formation was wet and humid, supporting an abundant and diverse range of organisms.
facts.quote: The climate was wet and humid, and supported an abundant and diverse range of organisms

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus is a genus of ornithopod hadrosaurid dinosaur, with a name meaning "near the crested lizard".
facts.quote: Parasaurolophus (del gr. para/παρα "junto" o "cerca", saurus/σαυρος "lagarto" y lophos/λοφος "cresta" significa "Cercano al lagarto crestado") es un género de dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 76 and 73 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico Superior, entre 76 a 73 millones de años, en el Campaniano, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus was a herbivore that walked both bipedally and quadrupedally.
facts.quote: Fue un herbívoro que caminaba tanto de manera bípeda como cuadrúpeda

facts.statement: Three species of Parasaurolophus are known: P. walkeri (the type species), P. tubicen, and P. cyrtocristatus (the short-crested species).
facts.quote: Se conocen tres especies, Parasaurolophus walkeri, la especie tipo, Parasaurolophus tubicen y la de cresta corta Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus was first described in 1922 by William Parks based on a skull found in Alberta.
facts.quote: Descrito por primera vez en 1922 por William Parks a partir de un cráneo hallado en Alberta

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus is known for its large, elaborate cranial crest shaped like a tube projecting backward and upward from the skull.
facts.quote: Este género es conocido por su gran y elaborada cresta craneal, con la forma de un tubo que se proyecta hacia atrás y arriba del cráneo

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus is one of the rarest duck-billed dinosaurs, known only from a handful of good specimens.
facts.quote: Es uno de los dinosaurios de pico de pato más raros, conocido solamente de un puñado de buenos especímenes

facts.statement: The function of the Parasaurolophus crest has been debated, with current consensus suggesting it was used for visual species and sex recognition, acoustic resonance, and thermoregulation.
facts.quote: La cresta ha sido objeto de muchas discusiones entre los paleontólogos, siendo el consenso actual que las funciones importantes de esta incluyeron el reconocimiento visual de la especie y del sexo, resonancia acústica, y termorregulación

facts.statement: The type specimen of Parasaurolophus walkeri is estimated to have a body length of 10 meters.
facts.quote: El largo del cuerpo del espécimen tipo de P. walkeri se estima en 10 metros.

facts.statement: The skull of P. walkeri measures 1.6 meters long including the crest, while P. tubicen has a longer skull indicating it was a larger animal.
facts.quote: El cráneo mide 1,6 metros de largo, incluyendo la cresta, sin embargo el cráneo de P. tubicen supera de largo, lo que indica un animal aún más grande.

facts.statement: The estimated weight of Parasaurolophus is 2.5 tons.
facts.quote: El peso estimado es de 2,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: The femur of P. walkeri measures 103 centimeters and is robust compared to other hadrosaurs of similar length.
facts.quote: El fémur mide 103 centímetros en P. walkeri y es robusto para su longitud cuando es comparado al de los otros hadrosáuridos.

facts.statement: Like other hadrosaurs, Parasaurolophus likely walked on both two and four legs.
facts.quote: Como otros hadrosáuridos, es posible que caminara tanto en dos como en cuatro patas.

facts.statement: Skin impressions from P. walkeri show a uniform structure of scales similar to tubercles with no special features.
facts.quote: Las impresiones de la piel que son conocidas en P. walkeri, muestran una estructura uniforme de escamas similares a tubérculos, pero sin ninguna particularidad en especial.

facts.statement: The long, side-flattened tail suggests that Parasaurolophus could swim.
facts.quote: Estos animales tenían la cola larga y aplastada a los lados lo que lleva a pensar que Parasaurolophus podía nadar.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the foot tips of Parasaurolophus were hooves or claws worn down by time.
facts.quote: El final de las extremidades es un misterio, algunos paleontólogos dicen que son pezuñas y otros dicen que son garras desgastadas por el tiempo.

facts.statement: The most remarkable feature of Parasaurolophus is its crest, which projects from the back of the head and is composed of the premaxilla and nasal bones.
facts.quote: Lo más remarcable de este dinosaurio es la cresta, la cual se despega de la parte posterior de la cabeza y estaba compuesta del hueso premaxilar y el nasal.

facts.statement: Many hypotheses have been proposed to explain the function of the crest, though most have been discredited.
facts.quote: Se han propuesto muchas hipótesis para explicar la función de la cresta, aunque la mayoría de ellas han sido desacreditadas.

facts.statement: The crest is believed to have been used for sexual attraction, communication during danger or orders, and thermoregulation.
facts.quote: Se cree que era para la atracción y distinción entre machos y hembras, para comunicarse en caso de algún peligro u orden y para termorregulación.

facts.statement: The most prominent theory is communication; internal structure observations suggest the crest functioned as a natural resonator for sound production.
facts.quote: La más sobresaliente es la de la comunicación. Esta se realizó observando la estructura interna del tubo, para concluir que pudo funcionar como un resonador natural, y haber tenido una función sonora.

facts.statement: While P. walkeri and P. tubicen had long crests with slight curvature, P. cyrtocristatus had a short crest with a more circular profile.
facts.quote: Como P. walkeri y P. tubicen tenía crestas largas con solamente una curvatura leve, P. cyrtocristatus tenía una cresta corta con un perfil más circular.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus was quickly assigned to the hadrosaurid subfamily Lambeosaurinae, whereas Saurolophus is considered a Hadrosaurinae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, rápidamente fue asignado a la subfamilia de hadrosáuridos Lambeosaurinae mientras que Saurolophus es considerado un Hadrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Its closest relative appears to be Charonosaurus, a lambeosaurine with a similar skull from the Amur River region in northeastern China, and both are placed in the tribe Parasaurolophini.
facts.quote: Su pariente más cercano parece ser Charonosaurus, un lambeosaurino con un cráneo similar, pero del que no se conoce la cresta completa, de la región del Río Amur en el noreste de China, y los dos son colocado en la tribu Parasaurolophini.

facts.statement: P. cyrtocristatus is considered the most phylogenetically basal of the three known Parasaurolophus species, or it could be a juvenile or female of P. tubicen.
facts.quote: P. cyrtocristatus, con su corta y redondeada cresta, es considerado el más filogeneticamente basal de las tres especies conocidas de Parasaurolophus, o podría ser un juvenil o hembra de la especie P. tubicen.

facts.statement: It had hundreds of teeth arranged in columns that were replaced as they wore down.
facts.quote: Tenía cientos de dientes ordenados en columnas que los iba reemplazando a medida que se desgastaban.

facts.statement: This wear was due to a sophisticated masticatory apparatus that allowed it to grind food before swallowing, unlike other herbivores of its time.
facts.quote: Este desgaste se debía a que tenía un sofisticado aparato masticatorio que le permitía moler el alimento antes de tragarlo, a diferencia de otros herbívoros de su época.

facts.statement: This animal fed up to four meters off the ground.
facts.quote: Este animal comía hasta los cuatro metros del suelo.

facts.statement: The juvenile specimen was discovered in the Kaiparowits Formation in 2009.
facts.quote: El juvenil fue descubierto en la Formación Kaiparowits en 2009.

facts.statement: The juvenile was identified as being about one year old when it died.
facts.quote: El juvenil ha se ha identificado como de alrededor de un año cuando murió.

facts.statement: Specimen RAM 14000 is the most complete and youngest Parasaurolophus ever found, measuring 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: El juvenil, bajo el número de espécimen RAM 14000, es el Parasaurolophus más completo y más joven jamás encontrado, y mide 2,5 metros.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus lived approximately 75 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años.

facts.statement: With only 25% of adult size, juveniles show that crest growth in Parasaurolophus began earlier than in related genera like Corythosaurus.
facts.quote: Con el 25% del tamaño total de los adultos, los juveniles muestran que el crecimiento de la cresta de Parasaurolophus comenzó antes que en géneros relacionados, como Corythosaurus.

facts.statement: Its age indicates that Parasaurolophus had a very rapid growth rate, occurring in approximately one year.
facts.quote: Su edad también significa que Parasaurolophus tuvo una tasa de crecimiento muy rápida, que tuvo lugar en aproximadamente un año.

facts.statement: The large crest of Parasaurolophus served as a visual signal to distinguish it from other contemporary dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Como un objeto grande, la cresta tiene un claro valor como señal visual y distingue a este animal de sus contemporáneos.

facts.statement: The crest allowed Parasaurolophus to identify similar dinosaurs like Corythosaurus and Lambeosaurus, as well as recognize the sex and age of individuals of its own species based on size and shape.
facts.quote: la cresta de Parasaurolophus le permitiría identificarse de otros dinosaurios similares como Corythosaurus o Lambeosaurus y reconocer el sexo y la edad de otro de su especie por el tamaño y la forma.

facts.statement: The skeleton of Parasaurolophus walkeri shows a V-shaped notch or gap in the vertebrae at the base of the neck.
facts.quote: El esqueleto muestra una brecha o muesca en forma de V en las vértebras en la base del cuello.

facts.statement: The presence of multiple injuries in a single individual is a rare observation that has the potential to reveal new information about the biology and behavior of these ornithopods.
facts.quote: La presencia de varias lesiones en un solo individuo es una observación rara y, en comparación con una importante base de datos de lesiones paleopatológicas de hadrosáuridos, tiene el potencial de revelar nueva información sobre la biología y el comportamiento de estos ornitópodos.

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus belongs to the parent group Parasaurolophini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Parasaurolophini

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Parasaurolophus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 20
